problem: Prior VLN agents on R2R (Seq2Seq, RCM, EnvDrop, Self-Monitoring, Regretful, AuxRN) perceive the scene passively and must commit to a navigation action at every step. Ambiguous instructions (e.g., two doors in a bathroom) and partial observability therefore produce random, low-confidence decisions. None of them can deliberately gather more visual information before committing.
motivation: When humans are unsure which way an instruction means, they first peek down the candidate directions, then make a confident choice. The authors add this ability to a VLN agent. They also observe that even a hard-coded one-step look into every neighbor raises success rate by several points, which suggests extra visual context from nearby viewpoints is highly informative.
key_idea: Add a learned, recurrent exploration module that decides when and which directions to explore and how far, aggregates what it sees into a knowledge memory, and residually updates the candidate-view features before the navigation decision; it is trained with IL plus an A2C reward equal to the improvement in the navigation decision.
insight: Ablations (Table 3, val-unseen) separate the components. Naive 1-step exploration of all directions gives SR 52→54 but TL 10.7→35.7 and SPL 48→16. Learning where to explore keeps SR at 55 with TL 13.7 / SPL 42. Multi-step exploration in all directions reaches SR 60 but TL 58.8 / SPL 12. The full selective multi-step model (at most 4 steps) gives SR 58, TL 20.6, SPL 40; going to 6 steps brings no SR gain (58) and lowers SPL to 38. So the SR gain comes from seeing beyond the immediate neighbors, while learned exploration decisions and the memory-based 'lazy' movement keep the path cost tolerable. Without the lazy strategy TL is 44.5 and SPL 18. Exploration happens at only 15.3% of steps, and the exploration IL and RL losses are complementary: removing either drops val-unseen SR to 53 or 55, versus 58 with both.
method: Basic agent: EnvDrop-style LSTM navigator over the panoramic action space; the action score is softmax(v_k^T W h_t) over the K navigable views.

Naive exploration: step one hop into each navigable view, attend over that viewpoint's navigable views using the navigation state, and residually update the view feature (v~ = v + W o^) before choosing the action.

Exploration-decision making: an exploration policy over the K views plus STOP (attention over the current views and the navigation state) picks which direction to explore, over repeated rounds; explored directions are removed from the candidates.

Deeper (multi-step) exploration: a recurrent exploration LSTM initialized from the navigation state chooses at each step to continue to a neighbor or STOP. Gathered attended features are stored in a knowledge LSTM whose final state updates the explored direction's feature.

Memory-based late action-taking ('lazy' strategy): visited views and their connectivity are stored in a memory graph so the agent 'imagines' returning rather than physically walking back. It moves only when it must reach an unvisited node, which cuts revisits and TL.

Training: navigation IL plus A2C (distance-change reward, ±3 at the end). Exploration IL imitates the teacher's next S actions. Exploration A2C uses as reward the navigation reward after exploration minus before, split evenly across steps, with a -0.1 per-step penalty.
Curriculum on the maximum exploration length (1→2→…→6 steps), about ×8 faster convergence; back-translation augmentation with a speaker on 176k synthetic routes, used for fine-tuning.

setting.backbone: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-152 features + LSTM navigator/exploration/knowledge modules (EnvDrop-based), trained from scratch
setting.training_data: R2R train set; fine-tuned on back-translation data (speaker-generated instructions for 176k unlabeled routes in R2R training environments). Pre-explore variant: additionally fine-tuned on speaker-synthesized instructions for routes sampled in the unseen test environments.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views as ResNet-152 features + 4-d orientation)
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (panoramic action space), plus exploration actions (explore a navigable neighbor / STOP exploration)
setting.privileged: none in single-run (the agent physically explores neighboring viewpoints, and these routes are counted in TL/SPL); the pre-explore setting accesses the unseen test environments beforehand; beam search scores multiple candidate routes with the speaker

TL and SPL count both navigation and exploration routes. Ablation variants on val splits are omitted: at most 1-, 3- and 6-step exploration; the naive model; multi-step exploration in all directions (val-unseen SR 0.60 / SPL 0.12); training-loss ablations; w/o lazy strategy (val-unseen TL 44.5, SPL 0.18). The 4-step full-model ablation row equals Ours*.
results: In single-run R2R, the agent reaches SR 58% on val-unseen and 60% on test-unseen, beating AuxRN (55/55) and EnvDrop (52/51). Its SPL (40/41) is lower than AuxRN (50/51) and EnvDrop (48/47), because exploration routes are counted and push TL to ~21. It also tops the leaderboard in the pre-explore setting (test SR 70, SPL 68 vs AuxRN 68/65) and in beam search (SR 71 with TL 176.2 vs EnvDrop 69 / 686.8).
limitations: Exploration steps inflate trajectory length: TL ~20 vs ~11 for the basic agent. SPL falls below the non-exploring baseline, so the SR gains are partly bought by local test-time look-ahead.

The exploration module attends mainly to the instruction for the current action and does not dynamically parse later instructions, so it can miss key landmarks during exploration (failure case analysis).
Relies on nav-graph connectivity and physically visiting neighbors; exploration depth is capped at 6 steps by GPU memory and time, and 4→6 steps brings no SR gain.
